new_statements.translation: Tonal realization rules generate these surface tonal units from underlying representations in which only two tonemes figure: high and low. [...] Koro can thus be described on the hypothesis of two underlying tonemes, high and low, which combine structurally to give tonal schemes very similar to those of the other Manding varieties. [...] The monosyllabic lexemes recorded all show either the tonal scheme H or the tonal scheme L(h) [...] Disyllabic lexemes are distributed among the three schemes HH, LH and LL(h).

new_statements.relation_note: Full tonal sketch: 2 tonemes, lexical tone classes, 11 ordered tone rules incl. H- and L-spreading, downstep, floating tones, definite = floating L+H; no mention of stress/accent.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Koro (korokan) is a tone language: two underlying tonemes H and L; lexical tone schemes H / L(h) for monosyllables, HH / LH / LL(h) for disyllables, HHH/LHH/LLH for trisyllables, every lexeme must contain at least one final H (possibly floating); surface contours derive via tonal compactness, floating-H deletion, flattening of rising schemes, and Koro-specific rightward spreading of both H and L (rules R1-R11), yielding downstepped H and HL contour tones; the definite marker is a floating L+H. Nothing is said about word stress/accent.
new_statements.secondary_stress: not discussed (no stress statement at all)
new_statements.exceptions: non-lexeme units may have other schemes (B for pronoun à 'he/she', HBh for prohibitive kónè); automatic final raising/lowering of the last syllable of a like-tone sequence is noted (p. 83) and excluded from transcription; author stresses the corpus (one speaker, one session) is limited.
new_statements.identity_note: p. 81: 'Le korokan est un parler manding du Centre de la Côte d'Ivoire, localisé dans la partie Est du département de Mankono, avec comme centres relativement importants Tiéningboué et Bouandougou'; corpus recorded Dec 1983 at Wèdala, a village a few km from Tiéningboué (the same Koro test village, Wedala, used by Boone et al. 2000 for kfo). This is Koro/korokan of Tiéningboué = ISO kfo = koro1306, explicitly contrasted with the neighbouring koyaga of Mankono (koya1253). Not the Koro of Touba (korokakan) and not Nigerian Koro. | Title and p. 15: 'parler manding de la région de Tiéningboué'; 'le Korodugu (qui coïncide à peu de chose près avec l'arrondissement de Tiéningboué)'; distinguished from koyagakan of Mankono. = kfo / koro1306.

new_statements.quote: Il suffira d'indiquer ici que les monèmes du korokan se répartissent en monèmes de schème tonal haut (só "village", bésa "lézard") et monèmes de schème tonal descendant (sò "cheval", bèra "porc-épic", sisè "poule", tubabù "Européen"); dans ce cas, la place à laquelle est indiqué l'accent grave représente la façon dont le schème tonal descendant se réalise en fonction de la structure syllabique des monèmes.
new_statements.translation: It will suffice to indicate here that the monemes of Korokan divide into monemes with a high tonal scheme (só 'village', bésa 'lizard') and monemes with a descending tonal scheme (sò 'horse', bèra 'porcupine', sisè 'hen', tubabù 'European'); in the latter case the position of the grave accent [diacritic] shows how the descending scheme is realized according to the syllabic structure of the monemes.
